DIAGNOSIS READY: ACE Inhibitor-induced Cough (with incidental Right Lower Lobe Consolidation likely representing post-obstructive atelectasis or a separate, non-infectious inflammatory process). 

The timing of your new cough coinciding perfectly with starting an ACE inhibitor like lisinopril or enalapril is the strongest clue. While the chest X-ray showed consolidation, your normal white blood cell count and lack of fever make a typical bacterial pneumonia unlikely. I recommend stopping the ACE inhibitor immediately to see if the symptoms resolve, and we may need a follow-up CT scan to ensure the lung consolidation clears.
